summary: This Dockerfile builds a PHP 8.2 container for running browser automation tests. It sets up a non-root user with matching host permissions, installs Chrome and its driver from Google's testing repository, adds Composer for PHP dependency management, and prepares a working directory for test scripts.

explanations.4: ARG defines build-time variables that can be passed to Docker when building; DOCKER_UID is the user ID number we want inside the container to match the host user.
explanations.15: apt-get install with --no-install-recommends keeps the image smaller by skipping optional packages; the && chains commands so they only run if the previous one succeeds.
explanations.17: These cleanup commands remove package manager caches and temporary files that Docker would otherwise keep in the image, significantly reducing its size.
explanations.24: groupadd creates a user group with a specific numeric ID; the ${} syntax substitutes the build argument value we defined earlier.
explanations.25: useradd creates the actual user account with a home directory, specific UID and GID to match the host, and /bin/sh as the login shell.
explanations.30: This URL points to a JSON file listing all available Chrome versions and their download locations.
explanations.33: wget downloads the Google Chrome signing key and pipes it to apt-key so the system trusts Chrome packages; --no-check-certificate skips SSL verification.
explanations.46: This pipes the JSON response through jq to filter and extract just the Chrome browser download URL for the specific version and platform we want.
explanations.48: printf prints a colored message showing which chromedriver version was found; \e[0;105m and \e[0;0m are color codes for the terminal.
explanations.50: unzip -j extracts files directly to the target directory without creating subfolders, which flattens the archive structure into /usr/local/bin/chrome.
explanations.55: Similar to line 46, this extracts the download URL for the chromedriver (the automation driver) instead of the browser itself.
explanations.66: COPY --from pulls a file from the official Composer Docker image instead of building it ourselves, saving build time and space.
